messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: Maghrebian 8.2 year-old boy
Admission Date: [Date]
Discharge Date: [Date]
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course Summary:

The patient was admitted for evaluation due to moderate mental retardation, mild intellectual disability, hyperactive behavior, and partial secondary generalized epilepsy with persistent atypical absences and psychogenic episodes. The physical and neurological exam revealed no abnormal findings. The EEG showed abnormal discharges of slow waves and spikes and bi-temporally localized waves. The MRI study showed cortico-subcortical atrophy and corpus callosum hypoplasia. A high definition karyotype and metabolic panel results were normal.

Valproic acid was administered to manage the seizures and hyperkinetic behavior. The patient's condition improved, leading to his discharge.

The genetic study showed 116 bases deletion in genomic sequence of EN2 gene: 155462376–155462491 (G1 marker). The patient showed abnormalities in the transcription of the EN2 gene, that implies the deletion of 208 bases (between 1493 and 1719 bases of the complementary sequence, C4 marker).

The patient has been discharged with improved symptoms and has been advised to continue the medications prescribed by the treating physician. A follow-up visit has been scheduled to assess the patient's progress with regard to the aforementioned symptoms.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible is partial epilepsy with secondary generalisation and persistent atypical absences, shown by abnormal EEG discharges and treated with valproic acid. The intellectual disability, hyperactivity and EN2 deletion are underlying or coexisting findings rather than the main focus of care. Epilepsy belongs to chapter G, category G40.

CODE: G40
